The Government of India has introduced a number of agriculture schemes in India for modernising agriculture, increasing productivity and boosting farmer income. India is a rural country and agriculture is the main source of livelihood. Over half of India's population is directly engaged in agriculture for their livelihood. These schemes of agriculture in India span across various areas such as irrigation, insurance, credit, organic farming, digital markets, and income support. They also cover related industries such as animal husbandry, fisheries and horticulture.
Agriculture schemes in India is a highly relevant topic for
GS Paper III
Indian Economy and Agriculture.

Why Agriculture Schemes in India Are Important
The agriculture industry in India has a number of significant problems. These include water scarcity, low productivity, small land holdings and poor market access. The government formulates policies for agriculture in India to address all these issues. Each of the various schemes of the farmers has a clear objective in India. These two are contributing to food security and rural jobs. They also foster the development of the agri-startup ecosystem in India. A robust system of farmer schemes in India can change the face of the rural economy.
Key Contributions of Agriculture and Allied Sectors
The agriculture and allied sector in India provides several important benefits:
Food Security:
It ensures enough food grains for the growing population.
Employment Generation:
It creates jobs directly and indirectly in rural areas.
Rural Development:
It improves infrastructure and supports allied industries.
Income Support:
It supplements farmer income through subsidies and insurance.

Future  of Agri Startup India
The concept of agri startup India is growing rapidly. RKVY-RAFTAAR supports young people to start agriculture-based businesses. These businesses use technology to solve farming problems. Whether it's through the use of drones for crop monitoring or leveraging AI for soil testing, India's agri startup ecosystem is undergoing a transformation. Seed funding and incubation support is provided by the government. This generates job opportunities for the rural population and promotes innovation. It also attracts private investment into the agriculture sector.

UPSC FAQs on Agriculture Schemes in India
What are the most important agriculture schemes in India for UPSC?
The most important schemes for UPSC are PM-KISAN, PMFBY, PMKSY, e-NAM, PKVY, PM-AASHA and RKVY-RAFTAAR.
What is the difference between PM-KISAN and PM-KMY?
The PM-KISAN scheme is an income support program for farmers in India providing them with ₹6000 per year. PM-KMY is a pension farmer scheme in India giving ₹3,000/month after age 60.
How does PMFBY help farmers?
PMFBY is a farmers' scheme of providing compensation to farmers in the event of crop failure due to natural causes, pests or diseases at very low premiums in India.
What is agri startup India?
Agri start-up India is a name used to describe the government support under RKVY-RAFTAAR to promote young entrepreneurs for establishing technology ventures in the agriculture sector.
What is the PM-AASHA scheme?
The PM-AASHA is a scheme for the farmers in India which was introduced in 2018, where farmers will be paid at least the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for their produce collection.
